The Egyptians are human beings, not gods, and their horses are flesh, not spirit. The Lord will stretch out his hand, and the helper will be overthrown; the one being helped will also fall, and all of them will perish together.

For this is what the Lord said to me: As a lion or a young lion growls over the prey it has torn, and many shepherds shout at it, yet it is not frightened by their voices or shaken by their numbers, so the mighty Lord will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its heights.
Like birds flying overhead, so the mighty Lord will shield Jerusalem. He will shield and deliver it; he will support and help it.
Return, children of Israel, you who have intensified your rebellion.
For on that day people will reject the idols of silver and gold that your hands sinfully made for you.
The Assyrian will fall by a sword, a sword not belonging to men; a sword not belonging to warriors will devour him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will be subjected to tribute.
The rock where he dwells will pass away, and his princes will be shattered by the signal, says the Lord, whose light is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
Look, kings will rule in righteousness, and rulers will exercise authority with justice.
A man will be like a shelter from the wind, like a refuge from a rainstorm, like a stream of water in a thirsty place, and like the shade of a mighty rock in a weary land.
The eyes of those who see will not be dimmed, and the ears of those who hear will listen attentively.
The heart of the foolish will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerer will be quick to speak clearly.
They will no longer call a fool a ruler, nor will they call a worthless person a savior.
For the fool speaks foolishness, and his heart devises wrongdoing, to practice perversity and speak about error, to leave the hungry person empty and deprive the thirsty person of drink.
The worthless person's tools are evil. He devises schemes to ruin the poor with lying words and to ruin the needy person's plea in court.
But the noble person plans noble things, and he will stand firm in noble things.
Wealthy women, rise and hear my voice! Confident daughters, listen to my words!
You confident women will tremble for a year, because the grape harvest has failed; it has been delayed and has not come.
Tremble, wealthy women! Shake, you confident women! Strip yourselves bare and tie sackcloth around your waists.
Beat your breasts for the green growth of the field and for the vine and its fruit.
Thorns and brushwood will grow on the land of my people, in all the houses of joy and in the strong city.

For the temple has been forgotten, and the city's strength has been abandoned. The splendid houses have become caves forever, a place of thorns and a delight for wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks of sheep.
Until a spirit from on high is stirred up over us, and the wilderness becomes like a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a forest.
Justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will be bestowed in Carmel.
The work of righteousness will be peace, and the service of righteousness will be quietness and confidence forever and ever.
My people will live in a peaceful dwelling, in a home of confidence and a resting place of confidence.
Hail will come down on the forest, and the city will be brought low like a plain.
Blessed are you who sow beside every water, where the ox and the donkey tread.
Woe to you who plunder! You will not plunder, and the deceiver will not deceive you. When you wish to plunder, you will be plundered; when you wish to deceive, you will be deceived.
Lord, have mercy on us, for our hope is in you. Be our helper in the morning and our deliverer in a time of distress.
At the sound of your terror the peoples fled, and at your exaltation the nations scattered.
Now your plunder will be gathered like the gathering of caterpillars, like a swarm of locusts gathered together.
The Lord, who dwells on high, is exalted, and he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
Your time will be faithfulness, and your salvation will be in shelter. Wisdom and knowledge—the fear of the Lord is his treasure.
If he appears to them, they will wail loudly, and the messengers of peace will weep bitterly.
The paths are deserted, and travelers have ceased passing along the road. The covenant has been broken, the cities have been despised, and people have been disregarded.
The earth mourned and sat in mourning. Lebanon was disgraced and put to shame. Sharon became like a plain; Bashan and Carmel became desolate.
“Now I will rise,” says the Lord. “Now I will be exalted, and now I will be lifted up.
You will conceive thorns and give birth to stubble. Through your breath, fire will consume you.
The peoples will be burned like lime; like thorns gathered together, they will burn in the fire.
You who are far away, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge my might.”
The sinners in Zion were terrified, and trembling seized the godless. “Who among us can dwell with consuming fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting burning?”

The one who walks in righteousness and speaks honestly, who hates deceit and oppression, who shakes his hand free of accepting a bribe, who stops his ears so as not to hear, and closes his eyes so as not to see evil.
He will dwell on high, and his dwelling will be in a rocky stronghold. His bread will be supplied, and his water will be assured.
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty in distant lands.
Your heart will learn fear: “Where is the scribe? Where is the one who weighs? Where is the one who counts the towers?”
He will not look upon the mighty people, the people whose speech is difficult to understand, whose tongue stammers and cannot be understood.
Look at Zion, the city of our festivals. Your eyes will look upon Jerusalem, a prosperous dwelling, a tent that will not move, whose pegs will never be pulled up and whose ropes will never be cut.

For the Lord is a glorious name for us. He will be for us a bright place, brightness, and room on either side, where a ruler’s dominion will not reign, and no mighty one who is found will pass through it.
For the Lord is the judge, the Lord is the one who declares, the Lord is our king, and he is our savior.
Your ropes have come loose and are not secure. Your masts have tilted, and they have not spread the sail, until they divided the plunder, and a multitude of the lame carried off the spoils.
No inhabitant will say, “I am sick.” The people living in it have received sin [?], a place of judgment.
Come near, you peoples, to hear; pay attention, you nations. Let the earth and all that fills it hear, the world and all its inhabitants.
For the Lord’s anger is against all the peoples, and his fury against their entire army, to destroy them and hand them over to slaughter.
Their slain will be thrown out, the stench of their corpses will rise, and the mountains will melt from their blood.
All the hosts of heaven will melt, and the heavens will be rolled up like a scroll. All their host will fall like a leaf falling from a vine, and like an unripe fig from a fig tree.
For my sword will drink its fill in heaven. Look, it will come down upon the Edomites, upon the people condemned in judgment.

The LORD’s sword is full of blood; it is greased with blood and with the fat of fattened animals and goats, and with the fat of rams’ kidneys. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
Wild oxen will fall with them, and bulls with young bulls. The land will be drenched with their blood, and the dust will be greased with their fat.
For the LORD has a day of vengeance and a year of repayment for the judge of Zion.
Her streams will turn into pitch, and her dust into sulfur; her land will become burning pitch.
It will not be extinguished night or day, and its smoke will rise forever. It will lie devastated from generation to generation, and no one will ever pass through it.
Pelicans and hedgehogs will possess it; owls and ravens will live in it. A measuring line of devastation will be stretched over it.
There will be no joy there, nor will they proclaim a kingdom, and all her nobles will come to destruction.
Thorns will grow in her palaces, and nettles and thistles in her strongholds. She will become a dwelling for jackals and a grazing place for ostriches.
Spirits will meet apparitions there, and a demon will call to its companion. There Lilith has settled and found herself a resting place.
There the hedgehog nested, laid eggs, brooded, and hatched them in her shade. There the kites gathered, each with its mate.
Search the book of the LORD and read: not one of them is missing, and none needs to search for another. For he himself commanded with his mouth, and his Spirit gathered them.
He cast lots for them, and his hand divided measured portions among them. They will possess it forever and live in it from generation to generation.
The thirsty wilderness will rejoice, and the plain will exult and blossom like a lily.

It will exult with joy and praise. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, and the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD and the splendor of our God. Admonition and encouragement for the weak: the Savior is coming and will save them.
Be strengthened, weak hands, and be made firm, trembling knees.
Say to the fainthearted, “Be strong and do not be afraid! Look, your God is coming as an avenger. God the Savior is coming and will save you.”
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be opened.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the stammerer will be set free, for waters have broken forth in the wilderness and streams in the plain.
There will be pools in the desolate place and springs of water in the thirsty ground. Grass, reeds, and rushes will grow in the dwelling place of jackals.
There will be a path there, and it will be called the Holy Way. No uncleanness will pass along it, and there will be no road on it. Fools will not wander there.
No lion will be there, and savage beasts will not come up or be found there. The redeemed will walk there.
The LORD’s redeemed will return and enter Zion with praise. Everlasting joy will be upon their heads. They will attain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, king of Judah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
The king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem with a large army. He stood by the channel of the upper pool, on the road to the fuller’s field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him.
The Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence on which you rely?
You have said that you have words on your lips, counsel, and strength for war. Now, on whom do you rely, that you have rebelled against me?
Look, you are relying on Egypt, that broken reed of a staff, which enters and pierces the hand of anyone who leans on it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like for everyone who relies on him.”
And if you tell me, “We trust in the Lord our God,” what has Hezekiah gained by removing the high places and altars and telling Judah and Jerusalem, “You must worship before one altar”?
Now make a wager with my master, the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses if you have riders to mount them.
How can you turn back even one of my master’s least servants? Yet you rely on Egypt to give you chariots and horsemen!
Have I now come up against this land to destroy it without the Lord? The Lord himself told me, “Go up against this land and destroy it.”

Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, because we understand it. Do not speak to us in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people standing on the wall.”

The Rabshakeh said to them, “My master did not send me to you and your master to say these things, but to the men sitting on the wall, so that they will not eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you.”
Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in the language of Judah, saying, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, because he cannot rescue you.
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord by saying, ‘The Lord will certainly rescue us, and this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.’

Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: ‘Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you may eat from his own vines and fig trees and drink water from his own cistern,
until I come and take you away to a land like your own, a land of grain and oil, a land of olive trees and vineyards.’
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, ‘The Lord will rescue us.’ Have the gods of the nations rescued their respective lands from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they rescued Samaria from my hands?
Which of all the gods of these lands has rescued his land from my hands, that the Lord should rescue Jerusalem from my hands?”
They remained silent, and no one answered him, because the king had commanded, “Do not answer him.”
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported the Rabshakeh’s words to him.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and entered the house of the Lord.
He sent Eliakim, the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, dressed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, “This is what Hezekiah says: ‘Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and wrath, for the labor pains have come, but the woman giving birth has no strength.

Perhaps the Lord your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master, the king of Assyria, sent to insult the living God, and will rebuke him for the words that the Lord your God has heard. So make supplication and pray for the remnant that remains.’”
The servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, “Say this to your master: This is what the Lord says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the messengers of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.”
“Look, I will put a spirit upon him, and he will hear a report and return to his own land. I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.”
The Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had left Lachish.
He heard about Tirhakah, king of Cush, and he went out to fight him. When he heard, he sent messengers to Hezekiah.
Say this to Hezekiah, king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you when you say that Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.
“Look, you have heard everything the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, destroying them. And will you be rescued?
Did their gods rescue the nations that my ancestors destroyed—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, and those of Hena and Ivvah?”
Hezekiah received the letters from the messengers and read them. Then he went up to the house of the Lord, and Hezekiah spread them out before the Lord.
Hezekiah prayed before the Lord and said:
“Lord Almighty, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
Incline your ear, Lord, and hear. Open your eyes, Lord, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, which he sent to insult the living God.
Truly, Lord, the kings of Assyria have devastated all the lands and their own land.
They burned their gods in the fire, because they were not gods but the work of human hands, made of wood, silver, and stone. So they destroyed them.
Now, Lord our God, save us from his hands, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are God.”
Isaiah son of Amoz was sent to Hezekiah and said to him, “This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: I have heard everything you prayed before me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria.
This is the word the Lord has spoken against him: ‘The virgin daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you. The daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
Whom have you insulted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

Through your messengers you have insulted the Lord and said, “With my many chariots I will climb the mountain heights and the slopes of Lebanon. I will cut down its tall cedars and its choicest cypresses. I will enter its highest reaches, the forest of Carmel.
I will dig and drink water, and with the hooves of my horses I will dry up all the mighty rivers.”
Have you not heard that I did this long ago and prepared it in ancient days? Now I have brought it about, so that it becomes ruin and desolation, like fortified cities.

Their inhabitants lost their strength; they were shattered and ashamed. They became like grass in the field, like tender green growth, like grain on rooftops, and like blighted grain before it stands tall.
I know where you sit, when you come in and when you go out, and how you have acted insolently before me.
Because you have acted insolently before me and your blasphemy has reached my ears, I will put a ring in your nose and a bridle between your lips, and turn you back along the road by which you came.’

“This will be the sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself, and in the second year what springs up from that. In the third year you will sow and reap, plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
The remnant of the house of Judah who survive will again be like a root that reaches downward and bears fruit upward.
For a remnant will come out of Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord Almighty will accomplish this.
Therefore this is what the Lord says concerning the king of Assyria: ‘He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow there. He will not advance against it with shields or set ambushes against it.
Instead, he will return along the road by which he came, and he will not enter this city,’ says the Lord.
‘I will defend this city and save it for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.’”
The angel of the Lord went out and struck down one hundred eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp. When people rose early in the morning, there they all were—dead bodies.
Sennacherib departed and returned home, and he lived in Nineveh.

While he was worshiping in the temple of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword. They fled to the land of the people of Corduene, and his son Esarhaddon became king after him.

In those days Hezekiah became deathly ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, “This is what the Lord says: Put your household in order, because you are going to die; you will not live.”
Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall, and Hezekiah prayed before the Lord.
He said, “Please, Lord, remember that I have walked before you faithfully and wholeheartedly, and have done what is good in your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying:
“Go and tell Hezekiah king of Judah: This is what the Lord, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Look, I am adding fifteen years to your life.
I will rescue you and this city from the hands of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
This will be your sign from the Lord that the Lord will do what he has said:
Look, I will make the shadow on the steps, which the sun has moved down on the steps of your father Ahaz, go back ten steps.” And the sun went back ten steps on the steps it had descended.
The writing of Hezekiah, king of Judah, when he became sick and recovered from his illness.
I said, “In the middle of my days I am going through the gate of Sheol; I have left behind the rest of my years.”
I said, “I will not see the Lord in the land of the living. I will no longer see human beings among those who dwell in the dust.”

My dwelling has been taken away and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent. My life has been cut short like a weaver’s work, like a web about to be cut off. From day until night you have brought me to an end.
I chirped like a chirping swallow and moaned like a dove. I lifted my eyes to the heights: “Lord, rescue me and restore me.”
What can I say? He spoke to me, and he passed on and drove away all my sleep because of the bitterness of my soul.
Lord, people live by these things; because of these things my spirit lives. Heal me and let me live.
Look, for my well-being I suffered bitter anguish. But you took delight in my life, so that it would not waste away in destruction, because you have thrown all my sins behind your back.
For Sheol will not thank you, nor will death praise you. Those who go down to the pit will not hope in your faithfulness.
Instead, the living will thank you, as I do today, and a father will make your faithfulness known to his children.
The Lord will save us, and we will sing his praises all the days of our lives in the house of the Lord.
Isaiah said, “Let them take a cake of figs and put it on the boil, and he will recover.”
Hezekiah said, “What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the Lord?”
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and gifts to Hezekiah, because he had heard that Hezekiah had been ill, had regained his strength, and had recovered.

Hezekiah was delighted with them and showed them his treasury—the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, his entire armory, and everything found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his house or throughout his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.

The prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and said to him, “What did these men say to you, and where did they come from to visit you?” Hezekiah said, “They came to me from the distant land of Babylon.”
He said, “What did they see in your house?” Hezekiah said, “They saw everything in my house. I left nothing in my house that I did not show them.”
Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the Lord Almighty:

Look, the days are coming when everything in your house will be taken away, and the treasure your ancestors have accumulated until today will go to Babylon. Nothing will be left for you, says the Lord.
Some of your sons who come from you, whom you will father, will be taken away and will become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the Lord that you have spoken is good. Let there be peace and truth in my days.”
“Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God.
Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and proclaim to her that she has been filled with strength and has taken pleasure in sin, and that she has received from the Lord’s hand double for all her sins.
A voice cries in the wilderness: “Prepare a road for the Lord, and make straight paths for our God in the plain.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low. Uneven ground will become level, and difficult terrain will become a plain.
The glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all flesh will see it together, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.”
A voice says, “Cry out!” And he said, “What shall I cry out?” “All flesh is grass, and all its beauty is like the blossom of the field.
The grass has dried up and the blossom has withered, because the breath of the Lord has blown upon it. Such is the grass of this people.
The grass dries up and the blossom withers, but the word of our God stands forever.”
Go up onto the high mountains, Zion, bearer of good news! Raise your voice with strength, Jerusalem, bearer of good news! Raise it and do not be afraid. Say to the towns of Judah, “Here is your God!”
Look, the Lord God comes with might, and his arm is powerful. Look, his reward is with him, and his work is before him.
Like a shepherd who tends his flock, he gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them against his chest, and he feeds the nursing ewes.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, measured the heavens with his span, measured the dust of the earth in his fist, and weighed the mountains with weights and the hills in a balance?
Who has directed the Spirit of the Lord, or who has been his counselor?
Whom did he consult, who taught him, made him understand the way of justice, taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
Look, the nations are like a drop from a bucket and like a slight tilt of the scales, and the islands are scattered like ashes.
He does not consider Lebanon sufficient for burning, nor its animals sufficient for a burnt offering.
All the nations are considered nothing by him; he considers them destruction and desolation.
To whom have you compared God, and to what likeness have you likened him?
Is it an image that a carpenter has made, which a metalworker has overlaid with gold, and refined silver
he has fastened to it? It is selected wood that does not rot. He chooses a carpenter, who carves it with his skill and prepares an image that does not move.
Have you not heard? Have you not known? Has it not been told to you from the beginning? Have you not understood the foundations of the earth,
and the one who sits above the circle of the earth, whose inhabitants are like grasshoppers, who stretches out the heavens like a vault and spreads them out like a tent to live in?
He makes rulers nothing and the judges of the earth as though they did not exist.
They will not be planted or sown or put down roots in the earth. He will blow upon them, and they will dry up, and a whirlwind will carry them away like stubble.
“To whom have you compared me, that I should be his equal?” says the Holy One.

Lift your eyes to the heights and see who created these things, who brings out their hosts by number and calls them all by name. Because of his great majesty and his mighty strength, not one goes astray.
Why do you speak, Jacob, and say, Israel, “My ways are hidden from the LORD, and my case is overlooked by my God”?
Have you not known? Have you not heard? The LORD is God forever, the one who created the ends of the earth. He does not grow weary or become tired, and his understanding cannot be fathomed.
He gives strength to the weary and increases the strength of those suffering pain.
Young men will grow weary and become tired, and warriors will surely stumble.
But those who hope in the LORD will renew their strength. They will grow wings like a dove. They will run and not become tired; they will walk and not grow weary.
Be silent, islands! Let the nations renew their strength. Let them approach and then speak; let them come forward together for judgment.

Who stirred up righteousness from the east and called it to his feet? Nations will be handed over before him, and kings will be broken. He will make his sword like dust and his bow like a falling bow [?].
He will pursue them and make peace, and he will not enter a road on foot.
Who prepared and accomplished this? The one who called the generations from the beginning. I am the LORD, the first and the last; I am he.
The islands saw me and were afraid. The ends of the earth were afraid; they drew near and came.
Each helps his companion and says to his brother, “Be strong!”
The carpenter encouraged the metalworker, who shapes with a hammer and works. He says of the joint, “It is good,” and they secure it with nails so that it will not move.
But now, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham, my friend,
whom I strengthened from the ends of the earth and called from its watchposts, I said to you, “You are my servant.” I chose you and did not reject you.
Do not be afraid, because I am with you. Do not be alarmed, because I am your God. I have strengthened you and helped you; I have also upheld you with my righteous right hand.
Those who hate you will be ashamed and disgraced. The men who contend with you will become nothing and perish.
You will look for them but will not find them—the men who contend with you. The men who fight against you will be as though they did not exist.
For I am the LORD your God, who strengthens your right hand. I have said to you, “Do not be afraid; I am your helper.”
Do not be afraid, you worm Jacob, you company of Israel. I am your helper, says the LORD, and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
Look, I have made you like a new threshing roller that grinds and crushes. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and you will make the hills like chaff.
You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away; the whirlwind will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD and boast in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and afflicted seek water, but there is none; their tongues are dry with thirst. I, the LORD, the God of Israel, will answer them and will not abandon them.
I will open rivers in the mountains and springs in the valleys. I will turn the wilderness into pools of water and the thirsty land into springs of water.
I will put cedars, box trees, myrtle, and olive trees in the wilderness. I will set magnificent cypresses together in the plain.
So that they may see and know, consider and understand together that the hand of the Lord has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Present your cases, says the Lord; present your arguments, says the King of Jacob.
Let them come forward and show what is to happen. Show us what the former things were, so that we may take them to heart and know their outcome; or let us hear what is coming.
Show us the signs that are to come, so that we may know that you are gods. Do good or do harm, so that we may tell of it and see together.
Look, you are nothing, and your works come from destruction. Choosing you is an abomination.
I have stirred up someone from the north to come from the rising of the sun and call on my name. Rulers will come and be trampled like clay that a potter treads.
Who will declare it from the beginning, so that we may know and say that he is right? There is no one who declares it, no one who makes it heard, and no one who hears your words.
These are the beginnings of Zion, and I will give Jerusalem a messenger of good news.
I looked, but there was no one who considered these things, whom I could question and who could give me an answer.
Look, they are all nothing, and their works are empty. Their works are an empty wind.
Look, I have upheld my servant, and my soul delights in my chosen one. I have put my Spirit upon him, so that he may bring forth justice to the nations.
He will not shout or quarrel, and his voice will not be heard in the street.
He will not break a damaged reed or extinguish a flickering lamp. He will bring forth justice in truth.
He will not go out or flicker until he establishes justice on earth, and the islands will wait for his law.

This is what the Lord God says, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and everything in it, who gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those who walk on it:
I, the Lord, have called you in righteousness, taken you by the hand, strengthened you, and given you as a covenant for the people and a light for the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to bring the prisoner out of confinement, and those who sit in darkness out of prison.
I am the Lord, and that is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to carved idols.
I am declaring new things, and look, the former things have come. Before they sprouted, I made them known to you.
The Song of Isaiah. Sing a new song to the Lord, his praise from the ends of the earth, you who sail the sea, together with all that fills it, the islands and their inhabitants.
Let the wilderness and its villages rejoice, and let Kedar become meadows. Let those who live among the rocks sing praise, and let them shout from the mountain peaks.
Let them give praise to the Lord and proclaim his praises in the islands.
The Lord will go out like a mighty warrior, and like a man of war he will stir up his zeal. He will shout, show his might, and kill his enemies.
I have been silent for a long time; I will keep silent. I have held back. Like a woman in labor, I will gasp and lay waste all at once.
I will devastate mountains and hills and dry up all their strength. I will turn rivers into islands and dry up pools.

I will lead the blind along a road they do not know, and make them walk on paths they have not known. I will turn darkness before them into light and level the mounds. These things I have done, and I have not abandoned them.
Let those who trust in carved images turn back in utter shame, those who say to cast idols, “You are our gods.”
Listen, you deaf! Look carefully and see, you blind!
Who is blind but my servant, or deaf like my messenger whom I send? Who is blind like the ruler, and blind like the servant of the LORD?
I have looked often, but you do not pay attention; I have opened ears, but you do not listen.
For the sake of his righteousness, the LORD desired to make the law great and glorious.

But this is a plundered and trampled people. They are all ensnared [?] and hidden in prisons. They have become plunder, with no one to rescue them, and something to be trampled, with no one to bring them back.
Who among you will hear this, pay attention, and listen for what is to come?
Who handed Jacob over to be trampled, and Israel to be plundered? Was it not the LORD, because we sinned against him and were unwilling to walk in his ways, and did not obey his law?
He poured out on them his fierce anger and the violence of war. It burned them on every side, but they did not understand; fire blazed among them, but they did not take it to heart.
But now this is what the LORD says, who created you, Jacob, and formed you, Israel: “Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you and called you by your name. You are mine.
If you pass through the sea, I am with you, and the rivers will not sweep you away. If you walk on fire, you will not be scorched, and the flame will not burn you.
For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I gave Egypt in exchange for you, and Cush and Seba on your behalf.
Because you are precious in my eyes, you have been honored, and I have loved you. I have given people in exchange for you, and nations in exchange for your life.
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west.
I will say to the north, “Give them up,” and to the south, “Do not hold them back. Bring my sons from far away and my daughters from the ends of the earth.”
Everyone who is called by my name—I created him for my glory; I formed him and made him.”
Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and those who have ears but are deaf.

Let all the peoples gather together, and let the nations assemble. Who among you can declare this and make the former things known? Let them bring their witnesses and prove themselves right; let them listen and speak truthfully.

“You are my witnesses,” says the LORD, “and my servants whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was created, and after me none will exist.
I, I am the LORD, and there is no other besides me.
I declared, saved, and made things known, and there was no foreign god among you. You are my witnesses,” says the LORD, “and I am God.
Even from the first day, I am he. No one can escape from my hands, and who can reverse what I do?”
This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “For your sake I have sent to Babylon and brought all the fugitives, and the Chaldeans who boast of their ships.
I am the LORD, your Holy One, who created Israel, your King.”
This is what the LORD says, who makes a way through the sea and a path through mighty waters,
who brings out chariots and horses and a mighty army: they will lie down together and will not rise; they will go out like a flickering lamp.
Do not remember the former things or dwell on the things of old.
Look, I am doing something new! Now it will spring up, and you will recognize it. I will make a road in the wilderness and rivers in the wasteland.
The wild animals will praise me, the jackals and the ostriches, because I have provided water in the wilderness and rivers in the wasteland for my chosen people to drink.
This people whom I have chosen for myself will drink.
It was not you who called on me, Jacob, but I who called you, Israel.
You have not brought me lambs for your burnt offerings or honored me with your sacrifices. I have not enslaved you with offerings or wearied you with frankincense.
You have not bought fragrant cane for me with silver or satisfied me with the fat of your sacrifices. Instead, you have enslaved me with your sins and wearied me with your wrongdoing.
I, I am the one who wipes away your wrongdoing for my own sake, and I will no longer remember your sins.
Remind me; let us argue our case together. State your case, so that you may be justified.
Your first father sinned, and your rulers acted wickedly against me.
Your leaders defiled the sanctuary. I handed Jacob over to destruction and Israel to disgrace.
Now listen to me, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
This is what the Lord says, who made you, formed you in the womb, and helped you: Do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
For I will give water to thirsty ground and streams to dry land. I will pour out my spirit on your descendants and my blessings on your children.
They will spring up among the grass, like willows beside the water.
One will say, ‘I belong to the Lord,’ and another will call himself by Jacob’s name. Another will write on his hand, ‘The Lord’s,’ and take the name Israel.
This is what the Lord says, the King of Israel and its Redeemer, whose name is the Mighty Lord: I, I am the first, and I, I am the last. There is no God besides me.
Who is like me? Let him proclaim it, prepare, and declare what has happened since I established a people forever. Let them declare the signs that are coming.
Do not be afraid or alarmed. Did I not tell you long ago and make it known to you? You are my witnesses that there is no God besides me, and there is no mighty one whom I do not know.

All the craftsmen who make idols are worthless, and there is no benefit in the things they have desired to make. The craftsmen who made them testify that they neither see nor hear nor know. Therefore they will be ashamed.
Those who make gods and carve cast images in which there is no benefit.
Look, all their makers are craftsmen from among human beings. Let them all gather and stand together; they will be ashamed and disgraced together.
The craftsman who sharpens iron smooths it with a file, carves it with a chisel, and shapes it with the strength of his arm. He grows hungry and thirsty, drinks no water, and becomes exhausted.
The carpenter selects wood and measures it, fastens it with [?], carves it, and makes it in the likeness of a man, with human beauty, and sets it up in a house.
The wood that was cut from the forest, which grew through the rain.
It becomes fuel for people: they take some of it, warm themselves, and bake bread. They also make a god and worship it; they make a carved image and bow down to it.
They burned half of it in the fire, roasted meat over its coals, ate and were satisfied. They also warmed themselves and said, “Ah, I am warm! I have seen the fire!”
With the rest they made a carved god, bowed down to it, prayed to it, and said, “Save us, for you are our god!”
They did not know or understand, because the sight of their eyes and the understanding of their hearts were obscured.

They did not take it to heart, nor did they know or reflect and say that they had burned half of it in the fire, baked bread over its coals, roasted meat and eaten it, and made the rest into a wooden idol for themselves and bowed down to it.
Their heart feeds on ashes and leads them astray into error. They do not save themselves or say, “Our right hand has made a lie.”
Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I formed you to be my servant. From now on, Israel, do not forget me.
I have swept away your wrongdoing like mist and your sins like a cloud. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.

Sing praises, heavens, for the Lord has acted! Shout for joy, foundations of the earth! Break into joyful praise, mountains, and the forest and every tree in it, for the Lord has redeemed Jacob and has been glorified in Israel.

This is what the Lord says, who redeemed you, formed you in the womb, and helped you: “I am the Lord, who made everything. I alone stretched out the heavens and spread out the earth, from myself and for myself.
I frustrate the signs of soothsayers and make fools of their diviners. I turn the wise back and make their knowledge foolish.

I confirm the word of my servant and fulfill the counsel of my messengers. I say of Jerusalem, ‘It will be inhabited,’ and of the towns of Judah, ‘They will be rebuilt,’ and I will raise up its ruins.
I say to the deep, ‘Dry up! I will dry up your rivers.’
I say of Cyrus, ‘He is my shepherd, and he will fulfill all my wishes,’ saying of Jerusalem, ‘It will be rebuilt,’ and, ‘The temple will be completed.’”

This is what the Lord says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped so that nations will be subjected before him: “I will loosen the belts of kings, to open doors before him, and the gates will not be shut.
I will go before you and level the heights. I will break bronze doors and cut through iron bars.
I will give you treasures in darkness and hidden stores, so that you may know that I am the Lord, who called you by your name, the God of Israel.
For the sake of my servant Jacob and Israel my chosen one, I called you by your name and gave you a title, though you did not know me.
I am the Lord, and there is no other. Apart from me there is no God. I strengthened you, though you did not know me,
so that people may know, from the rising of the sun to its setting, that there is none besides me. I am the Lord, and there is no other.
I form light and create darkness; I make peace and create evil. I am the Lord, who has made all these things.

Rejoice, heavens above, and let the clouds shower down righteousness. Let the earth open, let salvation increase, and let righteousness spring up together with it. I am the Lord, who created these things.
Woe to anyone who disputes with his Maker—a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth! Does the clay say to the potter, ‘What are you making?’ and, ‘I am not the work of your hands’?
Woe to anyone who says to a father, ‘What are you fathering?’ or to a woman, ‘What have you conceived?’”
This is what the Lord says, the Holy One of Israel and its Maker, whose name is the Mighty Lord: “Ask me for signs concerning my children, and give me commands concerning the work of my hands.
I made the earth and humanity upon it. With my own hands I stretched out the heavens, and I commanded all their host.
I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will make all his paths level. He will rebuild my city and release my exiles, not for payment or a bribe,” says the Mighty Lord.

This is what the Lord says: Egypt’s labor and the merchants of Cush and Sheba, men of great stature, will come over to you and become yours. They will follow you and come over in chains. They will bow down to you and pray to you, saying, “God is in you, and there is no other god.”
Truly, you are hidden, the God of Israel and its Savior.
They were all ashamed and disgraced together, those who walk in disgrace and carve idols.
Israel’s salvation is in the Lord, the eternal Savior. You will never be ashamed or disgraced, forever and ever.

For this is what the Lord says, who created the heavens—he is God, who formed the earth and made it, and he established it. He did not create it in vain, but so that his creation might live in it: “I am the Lord, and there is no other.”
“I did not speak in secret, in a place in a dark land. Nor did I say to Jacob’s descendants, ‘Seek me in vain.’ I am the Lord, who speaks righteousness and declares what is right.
“Gather and come; draw near together, you who have escaped from the nations. Those who carry carved wood and pray to a god who cannot save have no knowledge.

“Declare it and bring it forward; take counsel together. Who announced this long ago, from the beginning? I am the Lord, and there is no other god besides me, a righteous God and Savior; there is none besides me.
“Draw near to me, all the ends of the earth, so that you may be saved, for I am the Lord, and there is no other.
“I have sworn by myself, and a word of righteousness has gone out from my mouth and will not return: every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will swear by me.”
They will say, “Righteousness is in the Lord,” and the mighty will go to him. All who are hostile to you will be ashamed.
“In me all Israel’s descendants will boast and be justified.”
Bel has fallen, and Nebo has toppled. Their carved idols have become numerous loads for animals and hungry livestock.
They toppled and fell together. They could not rescue their loads, and they themselves went into captivity.
“Listen to me, house of Jacob and all the remnant of Israel, who are carried in the belly and carried in the womb.
“Even to old age I am he, and even to advanced age I will carry you. I have made you, and I will bear you; I will carry you and rescue you.
To whom have you likened me and compared me?
[?] those who carry and bring gold out of their purses and weigh silver on scales hire a metalworker and make a god. They bow down to it and also pray to it.
They carry it on their shoulders, transport it, and set it in its place. It cannot rise from its place. They even pray to it, but it does not answer them or save them from their troubles.
Remember these things and consider them; take your wrongdoings to heart.
“Remember the former things from long ago, for I am God, and there is no other god; there is none like me.
“I declare the final things from the beginning, and from long ago the things that have not yet happened. I say, ‘I will establish my purpose and do everything I desire.’
I call a bird from the east, and from a distant land a man who will carry out my purpose. I have spoken, and I will bring it about. I have planned it, and I will do it.
“Listen to me, you stubborn-hearted people, far from righteousness.
I have brought my righteousness near to coming, and my salvation will not delay. I will give salvation in Zion and my glory to Israel.
“Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground, daughter of the Chaldeans; there is no throne. For you will no longer be called delicate and pampered.
“Take the millstones and grind flour. Remove your veil, cut off your white garments, uncover your legs, and cross the rivers.
“Your nakedness will be uncovered, and your shame will be seen. I will take vengeance on you, and I will not meet you as a man.”
Our Redeemer—the Lord Almighty is his name—is the Holy One of Israel.
Sit in [?]; enter the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, for they will no longer call you the mighty lady of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people, who defiled my inheritance, and I handed them over to you. But you showed them no mercy; you laid a very heavy yoke on the elderly.
You said, “I will be mighty forever.” You did not take these things to heart or consider the outcome.
Now hear this, you pleasure-loving woman who sits at ease and says in her heart, “I am, and there is no other. I will never live as a widow or know the loss of children.”
Both these blows will come upon you in one day: the loss of children and widowhood. They will come upon you suddenly, despite your many sorceries and your many magicians.
You trusted in your wickedness and said, “No one sees me.” Your wisdom and your knowledge led you astray, and you said in your heart, “I am, and there is no other.”
Disaster will come upon you at dawn, and you will not know it. Calamity will fall upon you, and you will not be able to avert it. Turmoil will come upon you suddenly, without your knowing.
Stand firm, then, with your magicians and your many sorceries, over which you have labored since your youth. Perhaps you will be able to benefit; perhaps you will grow strong.
You have worn yourself out with your many plans. Let the Chaldeans who study the heavens and the stars, and announce to you each month what is coming upon you, stand up and save you.
Look, they have become like straw that fire has burned. They cannot save themselves from the power of the flame. There are no coals for their fire, nor any glow to sit before.
Such have your merchants become to you, those with whom you have labored since your youth. Each has wandered off in his own direction, and there is no one to save you.

Hear these things, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and have come from the loins of Judah, who swear by the name of the Lord and invoke the God of Israel, but not in truth or righteousness.
For they are named after the holy city and rely on the God of Israel; the Lord Almighty is his name.
I declared the former things from the beginning. They came from my mouth, and I announced them. Suddenly I act, and they come to pass.
I know that you are stubborn, that your neck is an iron sinew and your forehead is bronze.
I declared it to you long ago; before it happened, I announced it to you, so that you could not say, “My idols did it; my carved images and my cast images saved me.”
You have heard and seen all these things. Will you not declare them? I have announced new things to you, things kept hidden until now, which you did not know.
They are being created now, not long ago. Before today you had not heard them, so that you could not say, “I already know them.”
You have not heard, nor do you know them. Your ears were not opened long ago. I know that you are utterly deceitful, and you have been called a wrongdoer from the womb.
For the sake of my name I will delay my anger, and I will preserve my praise for you and will not destroy you.
Look, I have refined you, but not with silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of poverty.
For my own sake I will act, so that I am not defiled. I will not give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I called. I am the first, and I am the last.
My hand established the foundations of the earth, and my right hand spread out the heavens. I call to them, and they stand together.
Gather together, all of you, and listen. Who among you declares these things? The Lord has desired to carry out his will in Babylon and among the descendants of the Chaldeans.
I have spoken, and I have also called. I have brought her and made her way successful.
Come near to me and hear this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret. From the time it happened, I was there. And now the Lord God and his Spirit have sent me.
This is what the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says: I am the Lord your God. I teach you not to do wrong, and I show you the way you should go.
If only you had listened to my commandments! Your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your descendants would have been like the sand, and the children from your body like its grains. His name would neither cease nor perish from before me.
Come out of Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! Announce this with a voice of praise; proclaim it and spread it to the ends of the earth. Say, “The Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob!”
He led them through desolate places and made water flow for them from the flint. He split the rock, and water flowed out.
“There is no peace for the wicked,” says the Lord.
Be silent, islands, and listen, nations from far away! The Lord called me from the womb; from my mother's belly he mentioned my name.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword and hid me in the shadow of his hand. He made me like a choice arrow and concealed me in his quiver.
He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.”
And I did not say to Jacob's descendants, “I have labored in vain and spent my strength on emptiness.” Surely my judgment is before the Lord, and my work is before my God.
Now this is what the Lord says, who formed me in the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him and gather Israel: I have been honored before the Lord, and my God has become my strength.

He said, “It is too small a thing for you to be my servant to restore the tribes of Jacob and bring back Israel's offspring. I have made you a light to the nations, so that you may be my salvation to the ends of the earth.”

This is what the Lord, the Holy One of Israel and its Redeemer, says to the one whose life is despised, who is despised by the people and by the servants of rulers: Kings will see and rise, and rulers will bow down to him, because of the Lord, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who chose you.

This is what the Lord says: At a time of favor I answered you, and on the day of salvation I helped you. I formed you and made you a covenant for the people and a light to the nations, to restore the land and inherit the desolate inheritances.
You will say to the prisoners, “Come out,” and to those confined, “Show yourselves.” They will graze along the roads, and their pastures will be along every path.
They will neither hunger nor thirst, and neither the heat nor the sun will harm them, because the one who has compassion on them will lead them and bring them to springs of water.
I will turn all the mountains into roads, and the paths will be raised up.
These will come from far away, and these from the north, and these from the sea and from the sea of Sinim.
Sing praise, heavens, and rejoice, earth! Mountains, break into joyful praise, because the Lord has comforted his people and had compassion on his afflicted ones.
But Zion said, “The Lord has abandoned me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”
Can a woman forget her infant and have no compassion on the child of her womb? Even if these women forget, I will not forget you.
Look, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands, and your walls are always before me.
Soon your children [?]; those who tore you down and destroyed you will leave you.
Lift your eyes and look around you: they are all gathering and coming to you. “As I live,” says the Lord, “you will wear them all like ornaments and adorn yourself with them like a bride.”
For your ruins, your desolate places, and your devastated land will now be too crowded with inhabitants, and those who devoured you will flee.
The children of your bereavement will again say in your hearing, “This place is too cramped for us. Make room for us to live.”
You will say in your heart, “Who bore these children for me? Look, I was bereaved and alone, exiled and wandering. Who raised these? Look, I was left all alone; where were these?”

This is what the Lord God says: Look, I am raising my hand toward the nations, and I will raise a banner for the peoples. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your guardians, and their noblewomen your nursing mothers. They will bow down before you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust from your feet. Then you will know that I am the Lord, and that those who wait for me will not be put to shame.
Can plunder be taken from a mighty warrior, or the captives of a powerful man be rescued?

For this is what the Lord says: The mighty warrior’s plunder will be taken away, and the powerful man’s captives will be rescued. I myself will judge those who judge you, and I myself will save your children.

I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh, and they will become drunk on their own blood as on new wine. Then all humanity will know that I am the Lord, your Savior and your helper, the Mighty One of Jacob.

This is what the Lord says: Where is the certificate of divorce with which I dismissed your mother? Or who is the creditor to whom I sold you? Look, you were sold because of your sins, and your mother was dismissed because of your wrongdoing.

Why did I come and find no one, and call with no one answering? Has my hand been cut short and held back? Or do I have no power to rescue? Look, with my rebuke I dry up the sea and turn rivers into a desert. Their fish rot for lack of water and die.
I clothe the heavens in darkness and make sackcloth their covering.
The Lord God has given me a tongue trained in instruction, so that I may make a word known and declare it to the weary. He awakens morning by morning; he gives me ears to hear instruction.
The Lord God has opened my ears, and I have not turned back or resisted.
I gave my body to blows and my cheeks to striking. I did not turn my face away from humiliation and spitting.
The Lord God has helped me; therefore I have not been put to shame. Therefore I have made my face like stone, and I know that I will not be put to shame.
For the one who vindicates me is near. Who will contend with me? Let us stand together. Who is my accuser? Let him approach me.
Look, the Lord God helps me. Who will condemn me? Look, they will all wear out like a garment; the moth will eat them.
Who among you fears the Lord? Let him listen to the voice of his servant. Whoever walks in darkness and has no light, let him hope in the name of the Lord and be saved through his God.
Look, all of you kindle fire and set flames blazing. Walk in the brightness of your fire and in the flame you have kindled. This has come to you from my hands: you will lie down in sorrow.
Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness and seek the Lord. Look to the rock from which you were cut and to the pit from which you were quarried.
Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah, who conceived you. He was only one when I called him, blessed him, and made him many.

For the Lord is rebuilding Zion and rebuilding all her ruins. He makes her wilderness like Eden and her plain like the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness will be heard within her, thanksgiving and the sound of singing.
Listen to me, peoples, and pay attention to me, nations, because a law goes out from me, and my judgment is a light for the peoples.
My righteousness has drawn near, and my salvation has gone out. By my arm the peoples will be judged. The islands wait for me and put their hope in my arm.

Raise your eyes to the heavens, and look also at the earth below. For the heavens will pass away like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will become like it. But my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness will not pass away.
Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people with my law in their hearts. Do not fear people’s reproach, and do not tremble at their insults.
For the moth will eat them as it eats wool and clothing. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation through all generations.
Awake, awake, and put on the strength of the Lord’s arm! Awake as in the former days, as in the generations of long ago. It was you, you who made a great cut and destroyed the dragon.
It was you who dried up the sea and the waters of the great deep, and made a road in the depths of the waters for the redeemed to cross.
The Lord’s redeemed will return and enter Zion with praise. Everlasting joy will be upon their heads. They will attain delight and gladness, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
“I, I am the one who comforts you,” says the Lord. “Who are you to fear a mortal human being, a human being who withers like grass?

You have forgotten the Lord who made you, who stretched out the heavens and established the foundations of the earth. You have lived in constant fear every day because of the fury of the oppressor, who was preparing to destroy. Where is the oppressor’s fury?
He was urging the mighty to destroy. They will not die and perish, nor will his bread run out.
I, I am the Lord your God, who rebukes the sea so that its waves grow quiet. The Mighty Lord is his name.
For I put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hands, when I stretched out the heavens and established the foundations of the earth and said to Zion, “You are my people.”
Wake up, wake up! Rise, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the Lord’s hand the cup of his wrath. You have drunk and drained the cup of staggering.
There is no one to comfort her among all the children she bore, and no one to take her by the hand among all the children she raised.
These two things have happened to you—who will grieve over you?—plunder and destruction, famine and the sword. Who will comfort you?
Your children have fainted and lie at the head of every street like a wilted beet. They are filled with the Lord’s wrath and the rebuke of your God.
Therefore hear these things, you who are afflicted and drunk, but not with wine.
This is what your Lord, the Lord, says, and your God will defend his people: “Look, I have taken from your hands the cup of staggering, the cup of my wrath. You will never drink it again.
I will put it into the hands of those who humiliated you, who said to you, ‘Bow down so that we can walk over you.’ You made your people like the ground, like a street for those passing by.”
Wake up, wake up, Zion! Put on garments of glory, Jerusalem, the holy city, for the uncircumcised and the unclean will never enter you again.
Shake off the dust and rise; sit down, Jerusalem. Untie the yoke from your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
For this is what the Lord says: “You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without money.”
For this is what the Lord God says: “My people first went down to Egypt to live there, and the Assyrian carried them away by force.
Now what have I here,” says the Lord, “since my people have been carried away for nothing? Their rulers howl,” says the Lord, “and continually, every day, they blaspheme my name.
Therefore my people will know my name on that day, because I am the one speaking. Here I am.”
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the one who brings news of peace, who brings good news and announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
Listen to your watchmen! They raise their voices and praise together, for they will see with their own eyes when the Lord restores Zion.
Rejoice and sing praise together, ruins of Jerusalem, for the Lord has comforted his people and redeemed Jerusalem.
The Lord has revealed his holy arm before the eyes of all the peoples, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
Leave, leave! Go out from there, and do not touch anything unclean. Go out from her midst and set yourselves apart, you who carry the Lord’s vessels.
For you will not go out in haste, nor will you leave in flight, because the Lord goes before you, and the God of Israel gathers you together.
Look, my servant acts wisely. He will be raised up, lifted up, and greatly exalted.
Just as many will be appalled at him, so his appearance is disfigured beyond that of a man, and his form [?] beyond that of human beings.
He will cleanse many nations, and kings will shut their mouths because of him. For they have seen what was not told to them, and they have understood what they had not heard.
Who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
He grew up before him like a young plant, like a root from dry ground. He had no imposing appearance or splendor. We saw that he had no imposing appearance, and we rejected him.
He was despised and humbled among men, a man of pains who knew suffering. We turned our faces away from him; we despised him and did not value him.
Truly, he endured our sufferings and carried our pains, yet we considered him stricken, struck by God and humbled.
He was being killed because of our sins and humbled because of our wrongdoing. The punishment that brought us peace was upon him, and by his wounds we will be healed.
We have all strayed like sheep, and each of us has turned his own way. The Lord caused the sins of us all to fall upon him.
He came forward and was humbled, and he did not open his mouth. Like a lamb he was led to slaughter, and like a ewe before its shearer he was silent and did not open his mouth.
He was led away from imprisonment and judgment. Who can recount his generation? For he was cut off from the land of the living, and some of the wicked among my people came against him.
A wicked man gave him his grave, and a rich man at his death, although he had done no wrong and there was no deceit in his mouth.
The Lord desired to humble him and make him suffer. A sin offering was laid upon his life, so that he might see offspring and prolong his days. The Lord’s will will prosper through his hand.
From the toil of his soul he will see and be satisfied. Through knowledge he will vindicate the righteous. He is the servant of many, and he will bear their sins.

Therefore I will give him a share among the many, and he will divide the plunder with the mighty, because he poured out his life to death and was counted among the wrongdoers. He carried the sins of many and interceded for the wrongdoers.

Sing praise, barren woman who has not given birth! Break into praise and rejoice, you who have not been in labor! For the children of the desolate woman are more numerous than the children of the married woman, says the Lord.
Enlarge the place of your tents, and stretch out the curtains of your dwellings. Do not hold back! Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your stakes.
For you will spread out to the right and to the left. Your descendants will inherit nations and settle in desolate towns.
Do not be afraid, for you will not be ashamed. Do not be humiliated, for you will not be disgraced. You will forget the shame of your youth and no longer remember the disgrace of your widowhood.
For your Lord does this for you; the mighty Lord is his name. Your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, will be called the God of the whole earth.
For the Lord has called you like an abandoned woman, distressed in spirit, and like a wife married in youth who is abandoned, says your God.
In a little anger I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you.
In great anger I turned my face away from you, but with everlasting compassion I have had mercy on you, says the Lord your Redeemer.
This is like the days of Noah to me: as I swore that the waters of Noah would never again pass over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.
For the mountains will be brought low and the hills will sink down, but my kindness will not depart from you, and the covenant of your peace will not pass away, says the merciful Lord.
You who are humbled and storm-tossed, who have not been comforted, look: I am making your stones of beryl, and I will establish your foundations with sapphire stones.
I will build your walls with jasper stones, your gates with crystal stones, and all your boundaries with choice stones.
All your children will learn to know me, and great will be the peace of your children.
You will be established in righteousness. Keep far from oppression, for you will not be afraid, and from destruction, for it will not come near you.
All who turn away from my hands will come to you, and you will be a place of refuge for your inhabitants.
Look, I created the craftsman who blows the bellows into the fire and finishes a tool for his work. I also created the destroyer to destroy.

No weapon fashioned against you will succeed, and you will condemn every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the inheritance of the servants of the Lord, and their vindication is from me, says the Lord.
Come, all who are thirsty, go to the water! You who have no money, go, buy and eat! Wine and milk without money and without payment!
Why do you weigh out money for what is not bread, and spend your labor on what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and you will eat good things, and your soul will delight in rich food.
Incline your ears and come to me. Listen to me, and your soul will live. I will establish an everlasting covenant with you, the sure mercies of David.
Look, I have made you a witness to the peoples, a ruler and leader of the nations.
You will call peoples you have not known, and peoples who do not know you will run to you because of the Lord your God, and because of the Holy One of Israel, who has glorified you.
Seek the Lord, and when you find him, call on him when he is near.
Let the sinner abandon his way and the wicked man his thoughts. Let him return to me, and I will have mercy on him, and to our God, who forgives abundantly.
For my thoughts are not like your thoughts, and my ways are not like your ways, says the Lord.
For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so my ways are higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For just as rain and snow come down from heaven and do not return there, but water the earth, make it produce and sprout, and give seed to the sower and bread for food,
so will my word be that goes out from my mouth. It will not return to me empty, but will do what I desire and accomplish what I sent it to do.
For you will go out with joy and depart in peace. The mountains and hills will rejoice before you with praise, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
Instead of the thornbush, the cypress will grow, and instead of the nettle, the myrtle will grow. This will bring renown to the Lord and be an everlasting sign that will not pass away.
This is what the Lord says: Maintain justice and do what is right, for my salvation is near to coming, and my righteousness to being revealed.
Blessed is the man who does this, and the human being who holds firmly to it, who also keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hands from doing evil.
Let not the foreigner who joins himself to the Lord say, “The Lord will surely separate me from his people.” And let not the eunuch say, “I am a dry tree.”
For this is what the Lord says to the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, choose what I desire, and hold firmly to my covenant:
I will give them, within my house and my walls, a place and a name better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not pass away.

And the foreigners who join themselves to the Lord to serve him, to love the name of the Lord, and to be his servants—all who also keep the Sabbath without profaning it and hold firmly to my covenant—

I will bring them to my holy mountain and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
This is what the Lord God says, who gathers the scattered people of Israel: I will gather still others to him, in addition to those already gathered.
Every wild animal of the field, come and devour all the animals of the forest!
The seers are all blind and know nothing. They are all mute dogs, unable to bark, dreaming and lying down, loving to slumber.
They are dogs with greedy appetites who never know satisfaction. They become evil and have no understanding. They have all turned to their own way, each to his own side and his own direction.
Come, let us get wine and get strong drink, and let it be as it is today, with a great deal more left over for us.
Look, the righteous man perishes, and no one takes it to heart. Devout men are gathered away without anyone understanding, for the righteous man is gathered away from the coming evil.
Peace will come, and they will rest on their beds and go straight ahead.
But you, come here, children of [?], adulterous and promiscuous offspring!
Whom have you mocked? Against whom have you opened your mouths and stuck out your tongues? Look, you are children of wickedness, offspring of falsehood.
You who find comfort in idols under every leafy tree, and slaughter children in the valleys beneath the rocky cliffs.
Your portion and your inheritance are with the portion of the valleys. To them you have poured out drink offerings and offered sacrifices. Should I be comforted by these things?
On high and lofty mountains you made your bed, and you also went up there to offer sacrifices.

Behind the doors and on the doorposts you have inscribed your memorial. For you have uncovered yourself away from me, climbed up, and enlarged your bed. You have become one of them, loved their bed, and looked out a place.
You gloried before kings with oil and multiplied your perfumes. You sent your messengers far away and lowered yourself as far as Sheol.
You grew weary with your many journeys, but you did not say, ‘I will stop.’ You grew strong in the guilt of your hands; therefore you did not plead for mercy.
Whom did you dread and fear, that you lied to me, did not remember me, and did not consider me in your heart? Look, I am the Holy One from eternity, yet you did not fear me.
I will reveal my righteousness, and your deeds will not benefit you.

When you cry out, let those who gather around you rescue you! The wind will carry them all away, and a whirlwind will sweep them off. But those who put their hope in me will inherit the land and possess my holy mountain.
They will say, ‘Clear it, clear it! Prepare the road! Remove the stumbling blocks from the road of my people!’

For this is what the High and Exalted One says, who dwells forever and whose name is holy: His dwelling is high and holy, and with the humble and those distressed in spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble and revive the hearts of those in pain.
For I will not contend forever, nor will I be angry forever, because the spirit goes out from me, and I made the breath of life.
Because of the wickedness of her deceit, I was angry and struck her. I turned away and was angry, but she went on wantonly in the way of her heart.
I have seen her ways and healed her. I have comforted her and restored comfort to her and to her mourners.
I create the speech of lips: ‘Peace, peace to those far away and those nearby,’ says the Lord, ‘and I will heal them.’
The wicked are troubled like the sea, because they cannot be still, and its waters toss up debris and mud.
‘There is no peace for the wicked,’ says my God.
Cry out at the top of your voice and do not hold back! Raise your voice like a trumpet. Declare to my people their wrongdoing, and to the house of Jacob their sins.

They seek me every day and desire to know my ways, like a nation that practices righteousness and has not abandoned the judgment of its God. They ask me for judgment and righteousness and desire to draw near to God.
‘Why have we fasted, and you have not seen? Why have we humbled ourselves, and you have not noticed?’ Look, on the day of your fast you do as you please and bring forward all your idols.
Look, you fast for quarreling and contention, and to strike with wicked force. Do not fast as you do today and expect to make your voice heard on high.
Is this the fast I have chosen: for a person to humble himself, bow his neck like a reed, and spread sackcloth and ashes beneath himself? Will you call this a fast and a day pleasing to the Lord?
This is the fast I have chosen: that you loosen the bonds of wickedness, cut the fetters of deceit, and release the oppressed into freedom, and that you break every fetter.
Share your bread with the hungry, and bring the stranger into your house. When you see someone naked, clothe him, and do not neglect your own flesh and blood.
Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your righteousness will quickly shine out. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the Lord will gather you together.
Then you will call, and the Lord will answer you. You will cry out, and he will say, ‘Here I am,’ if you remove deceit from your midst, release the oppressed, and keep away from speaking lies.
If you give your bread to the hungry and satisfy the hungry person, your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkness will be like midday.
The Lord will guide you continually, satisfy you with abundance, and strengthen your bones. You will be like a flourishing garden and like a spring of water whose waters never fail.

Those from among you will rebuild the ancient ruins, and you will raise up foundations from generation to generation. They will call you the one who closes breaches and restores paths for people to live along.

If you turn your foot away on the Sabbath, so as not to do as you please on my holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight and the Lord’s holy day honorable, and honor it by not going your own way on it, not doing as you please on it, and not speaking a word.
Then you will trust in the Lord, who will make you ride on the heights of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
Look, the Lord’s hand is not too short to save, nor is his ear too dull to hear.
But your wrongdoings have separated you from your God, and your sins have turned his face away from you so that he does not hear.
For your hands are stained with blood and your fingers with wrongdoing. Your lips speak lies, and your tongue devises injustice.
No one pleads a case justly, and no one judges faithfully. They trust in emptiness and speak worthless things. They conceive wrongdoing and give birth to suffering.
They hatch the eggs of venomous snakes and weave a spider’s web. Whoever eats their eggs will die, and whoever breaks one open finds a viper.
Their webs will not become clothing, nor will they cover themselves with what they make. Their deeds are evil deeds, and acts of injustice are in their hands.
Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are evil thoughts; plunder and destruction are in their paths.
They do not know the way of peace, and there is no justice in their ways. Their paths are crooked, and whoever walks in them does not know peace.
Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We wait for light, but there is darkness; for brightness, but we walk in gloom.
We feel our way along the wall like the blind; we grope like those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as though it were evening, and we groan like those who are near death.
We all growl like bears and moan like doves. We wait for justice, but there is none, and for salvation, but it is far from us.
For our wrongdoing is great before you, and our sins testify. Our wrongdoing is with us, and our sins are known.

We have acted wickedly and dealt falsely with the Lord, and we have turned away from following our God. We have spoken oppression and rebelled; we have conceived and pondered words of falsehood in our hearts.
We have turned justice backward and made righteousness stand far away, because truth has stumbled in the public square, and honesty cannot enter.
Truth has gone into hiding, and understanding has departed from our minds. The Lord saw that there was no justice, and it was evil in his eyes.
He saw that there was no one, and he was astonished that there was no one to help. His own arm saved him, and his righteousness sustained him.
