He put on righteousness like a breastplate, with a helmet of salvation on his head, and he put on a garment of vengeance,
to exact vengeance on those who hate him and repay his enemies. He will repay the islands what they deserve.
From the west they will fear the name of the Lord, and from the rising of the sun, his glory. For the oppressor will come like a river, and the Spirit of the Lord will bring him low.
A redeemer will come to Zion, and those who turn wrongdoing away from Jacob, says the Lord.

As for me, this is my covenant with you, says the Lord: My Spirit that is upon you and my words that I have placed in your mouth will not depart from your mouth, or from the mouth of your offspring, or from the mouth of your offspring’s offspring, says the Lord, from now and forever.
Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord will rise upon you.
For look, darkness covers the earth, and thick darkness covers the nations. But the Lord will shine upon you, and his glory will be seen over you.
Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.
Lift your eyes and look around you: they are all gathering and coming to you. Your sons will come from far away, and your daughters will be nurtured on the hip.
Then you will see and shine, and you will rejoice, and your heart will expand, because the wealth of the sea will turn to you, and the riches of the nations will come to you.
A caravan of camels will cover you, young camels from Midian and Ephah. They will all come from Sheba, carrying gold and frankincense and proclaiming the praises of the Lord.
All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you, and the rams of Nebaioth will serve you. They will be offered acceptably on my altar, and I will glorify the house of my glory.
Who are these who fly like clouds, like doves to their windows?

For the islands wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish, as in former times, to bring your children from far away, with their silver and gold, for the name of the LORD your God and the Holy One of Israel, who has glorified you.
Foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will serve you. For in my anger I struck you, but in my favor I have had mercy on you.
Your gates will remain open continually, day and night; they will not be shut. The wealth of the nations will be brought to you, with their kings being led along.
For the people and kingdom that will not serve you will perish, and the nations will be devastated by the sword.
The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the stately cypress and the pines together, to glorify the place of my sanctuary; and I will honor [?] the place of my feet.
The children of those who humbled you will come to you bowing down, and all who provoked you will bow at the soles of your feet. They will call you Zion, the city of the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
Instead of being abandoned and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you an everlasting glory, a joy from generation to generation.
You will suck the milk of the nations and suck the spoils of kings. Then you will know that I am the LORD, your Savior and your Deliverer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
Instead of bronze I will bring gold, and instead of iron I will bring silver; instead of wood, bronze, and instead of stones, iron. I will make peace your overseer and righteousness your ruler.
Injustice will no longer be heard of in your land, nor plunder and destruction within your borders. They will call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
The sun will no longer be your light by day, and the moon’s light will not shine for you, because the Lord will be your everlasting light.
And the days of your mourning will come to an end.
All your people will be righteous; they will inherit the land forever. The shoot that I planted, the work of my hands, will be glorified.
The smallest will become thousands, and the least a mighty nation. I, the LORD, will hasten it at its proper time.

The Spirit of the LORD God is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me and sent me to bring good news to the humble, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom to captives and release to prisoners,
and to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor and the day of salvation of our God, to comfort all who mourn,

to give those who mourn in Zion glory instead of ashes, fragrant oil instead of mourning, and a garment of praise instead of a sorrowful spirit. They will be called rams of righteousness, the glorious planting of the LORD.
They will rebuild the ancient ruins and restore the places devastated long ago. They will renew the ruined cities and the places devastated for generations.
Foreigners will stand and tend their flocks, and foreigners will be their farmers and vinedressers.
But you will be called priests of the LORD; you will be spoken of as ministers of our God. You will consume the wealth of the nations and glory in their splendor.
Instead of your shame and your disgrace, you will inherit a double inheritance in their land, and you will glory in their portion. Everlasting joy will be yours.
For I am the LORD, who loves justice and hates robbery and injustice. I will faithfully give you the reward for your labor and establish an everlasting covenant with you.
Your descendants will be known among the peoples, and your descendants' descendants among the nations. All who see you will recognize that you are offspring whom the LORD has blessed.

I will greatly delight in the LORD, and my soul will rejoice in my God, because he has clothed me in garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, like a splendid bridegroom and an adorned bride.
For as the earth brings forth growth and a garden makes seed sprout, so the LORD God will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations.
For Zion’s sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness comes forth like light and her salvation burns like a torch.
The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory. You will be called by a new name that the mouth of the Lord will give you.
You will be a glorious crown in the Lord’s hand, a royal diadem in the hand of your God.

You will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will no longer be called Desolate. Instead, you will be called My Delight, and your land Married, because the Lord delights in you, and your land will be married.
For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons will marry you; and as a bridegroom rejoices over a bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
On your walls, Jerusalem, I have stationed watchmen, every day, day and night, continually, so that they will not be silent or rest, those who bring reminders before the Lord.
Do not give them rest until he establishes you, until he makes you, Jerusalem, a source of praise on the earth.
The Lord has sworn by his right hand and by his mighty arm: “I will no longer give your grain to your enemies for food, and foreigners will not drink the wine for which you have labored.”
Instead, those who gather it will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who gather it will drink it in the holy courts.
Pass through, pass through the gate! Clear the way for the people! Prepare the road and remove its stones! Raise a banner for the nations!
Look, the Lord has proclaimed to the ends of the earth: “Say to daughter Zion, ‘Look, your Savior is coming! Look, his reward is with him, and his work is before him.’”
They will call them the Holy People, the Redeemed of the Lord; and you will be called Sought After, a City Not Forsaken.
Who is this coming from Edom, from Bozrah with his garments red, splendid in his clothing and mighty in his great strength? “It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save.”
Why are your garments red, and your clothes like those of someone treading a winepress?

“I have trodden the winepress alone, and no one from the nations was with me. I pressed them in my anger and trampled them in my fury. Their blood splashed onto my clothes, and I stained all my garments.
For the day of vengeance is in my heart, and the year of my deliverance has come.
I looked, but there was no one to help; I was astonished, but there was no one to support me. My own arm saved me, and my fury sustained me.
I trampled the nations in my anger and afflicted them in my fury, and I brought their strength down to the ground.”

I will recall the Lord’s kindness and the Lord’s praise, for all that the Lord has done for me. He lavished his kindness on the house of Israel, rewarding me according to his compassion and the abundance of his kindness.
He said, “They are my people, children who do not lie,” and he became their Savior.
In all their afflictions he did not afflict them, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his mercy and his tender care he redeemed them; he lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. He turned into their enemy, and he himself fought against them.
He remembered the days of old, of Moses his servant: how he brought up from the sea the shepherd of his flock, and how he placed his Holy Spirit within him.
His glorious arm led at Moses’ right hand. He split the sea before them and made an everlasting name for them.
He led them through the depths like a horse in the wilderness, and they did not stumble.
Like livestock going down into a valley, the Spirit of the Lord led them. In this way you led them, your people, and made a glorious name for yourself.
Look down from heaven and see from your holy and glorious dwellings. Where are your zeal and your might, the stirring of your heart and your compassion that you showed toward us?
For you are our Father. Abraham did not know us, and Israel did not acknowledge us. You, Lord, are our Father and our Redeemer; your name is from everlasting.
Why, Lord, have you made us stray from your way and hardened our hearts against fearing you? Return for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance.
Your holy people will possess it for only a little while. Our oppressors have trampled your sanctuary.
We have become like those over whom you never ruled, who were never called by your name. Did you not open the heavens and come down, so that the mountains shook before you?
And they melted as wax melts before fire. The fire will burn your enemies, and your name will be known to your enemies, and the nations will tremble before you.
When you did awesome things, we were not expecting you. You came down, and the mountains shook before you.
Since ancient times no one has listened or heard, and no eye has seen a God besides you, who acts for those who wait for you.
You gladly meet those who practice righteousness and remember you in your ways. Look, you became angry, and we sinned. Through them we will be saved forever.
For we have all become like unclean people, and all our righteousness is like a menstruating woman's rag. We have all fallen like leaves, and our sins have carried us away like a whirlwind.
There is no one who calls on your name or remembers to hold fast to you, because you have turned your face away from us and handed us over to our sins.
Now, Lord, you are our Father. We are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hands.
Do not be so very angry forever, Lord, and do not remember our sins forever. See that we are all your people.
Your holy cities have become a wilderness. Zion has become a wilderness, and Jerusalem a ruin.
Our holy and glorious house, where our ancestors praised you, has been burned with fire, and everything we cherished has become a ruin.
In the face of these things, Lord, have you held back, remained silent, and humbled us so greatly?
I was sought by those who did not ask for me, and I was found by those who did not seek me. I said, “Here I am, here I am,” to a people who did not call on my name.
I stretched out my hands all day long to a disobedient people, who follow their own thoughts along a way that is not good.
A people who continually provoke me, sacrificing in gardens and placing incense on stones,
who sit among graves and spend the night in caves, who eat pork and smear their vessels with carcasses, violating the law and defiling the holy covenant to provoke the Lord.
They say, “Go away! Do not come near me, because I am holy.” These have become smoke in my anger, a fire burning every day.
Look, it is written before me. I will not remain silent until I repay them double into their laps.
Their sins and their ancestors' sins [?], says the Lord. They placed incense on the mountains and insulted me on the hills. I will first measure out their deeds into their laps.

This is what the Lord says: Just as a berry is found in a cluster of grapes, and someone says to his companion, “Do not destroy it, because there is a blessing in it,” so I will act for the sake of my servants and will not destroy them all.
I will bring forth descendants from Jacob, and from Judah an heir to my mountain. My chosen ones will inherit it, and my servants will live there.
Sharon will become a fold for sheep, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for cattle, for my people who have sought me.
But you who have abandoned the Lord and forgotten his holy mountain, who have loaded tables for the gods of fortune and mixed drinks in bowls for them—

I will assign you to the sword, and all of you will kneel for slaughter, because I called and you did not answer; I spoke and you did not listen. You did what was evil before me and chose what I do not desire.
Therefore this is what the Lord God says: Look, my servants will eat, but you will go hungry. Look, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Look, my servants will rejoice, but you will weep.
Look, my servants will sing praise because of the gladness of their hearts, but you will groan because of the pain in your hearts and the brokenness of your spirits.
You will leave your name as a curse for my chosen ones. The Lord God will put you to death, but he will call his servants by another name.

Whoever invokes a blessing in the land will invoke a blessing by the faithful God, and whoever swears in the land will swear by the faithful God, because the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from my sight.
For look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered or come to mind.
Instead, they will rejoice and exult forever and ever in what I create. For look, I am creating Jerusalem as a joy, and I will rejoice in her.
I will rejoice in Jerusalem and exult in my people. The sound of weeping and the sound of wailing will no longer be heard in her.

There will no longer be an infant there who lives only a few days, or an old person who does not live out his days. For a young person will die at a hundred years old, and a sinner a hundred years old will be cursed.
They will build houses and live in them, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
They will not build for others to live in, or plant for others to eat. For the days of my people will be like the days of trees, and my chosen ones will eat the produce of their own hands.
They will not labor in vain or bear children for a curse, because they are offspring blessed by the Lord, they and their children with them.
Before they call, I will answer them, and before they speak, I will hear them.
The wolf and the lamb will graze together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox. Dust will be the serpent's food. They will neither harm nor destroy anywhere on my holy mountain, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord says: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool beneath my feet. What house will you build for me, or where is the place for my rest?
My hand made all these things, and all these things are mine, says the Lord. Whom will I look upon and dwell with except the gentle person, humble in spirit, who trembles at my word?

Whoever slaughters an ox is like someone who kills a man. Whoever sacrifices a lamb is like someone who kills a dog. Whoever offers fine flour is like someone offering pig's blood. Whoever offers frankincense is like someone who blesses idols. They have chosen their own ways, and their souls delight in their idols.

I too will delight in mocking them, and I will repay them for their deeds, because I called and no one answered; I spoke and they did not listen. They did what was evil in my sight and chose what I did not desire.

Hear the word of the Lord, you who tremble at his word. Say to your brothers who hate you and reject you because of my name, 'Let the Lord be glorified, and let us rejoice in your joy.' But they will be put to shame.
A sound of turmoil from the city, a sound from the temple—the voice of the Lord, who brings retribution upon his enemies.
Before she goes into labor, she gives birth; before her labor pains come upon her, she delivers a male child.

Who has heard of anything like this? Who has seen anything like these things: a land going into labor in one day, and a nation being born in a single hour? For Zion went into labor and gave birth to her children.
Have I given this hope and will I not bring about the birth? says the Lord. Am I not the one who brings about birth, and would I hold it back? says your God.
Rejoice in Jerusalem and exult in her, all who love her. Take delight with her, all who have mourned over her.
You will nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breast; you will nurse and be pampered by the abundance of her glory.
For this is what the Lord says: Look, I am pouring peace upon her like a river, and the glory of the nations like a sweeping torrent. You will nurse, be carried on hips, and be raised on knees.
As a man is comforted by his mother, so I will comfort you, and you will be comforted in Jerusalem.
You will see, and your hearts will rejoice; your bones will flourish like grass. The hand of the Lord will be revealed to his servants, and it will destroy his enemies.
For look, the Lord is coming with fire, and his chariot is like a whirlwind, to unleash his furious anger and his rebuke in a flame of fire.
For the Lord judges by fire, and by it he tests all humanity. Those slain by the Lord will be many.
Those who consecrate and purify themselves in the gardens, one after another in the middle, and eat pork, creeping things, and mice will perish together, says the Lord.
I know their deeds and their thoughts. When I come to gather all nations and languages, they will come and see my glory.

I will set a sign among them and send survivors from among them to the nations: to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow; to Tubal and Javan; and to the distant islands that have not heard my name or seen my glory. They will proclaim my glory among the nations.

They will bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the Lord, on horses, in chariots, and in wagons, to my holy mountain, to Jerusalem, says the Lord, just as the Israelites bring fine flour in clean vessels to the house of the Lord.
I will also take some of them as priests and Levites, says the Lord.
Just as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making will endure before me, says the Lord, so your descendants and your name will endure.
From month to month and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all humanity will come to worship before me, says the Lord.
They will go out and see the corpses of the people who rebelled against me. Their worm will not die, and their fire will not go out, and they will be an object of astonishment to all humanity.
